segments: 366. The Eleventh [dynasty].
he was found dead.
And when the people of Baghdad noticed,
they threw him down from the shoulders of the one who was carrying him,
and exposed him.
And they tied a rope to his member,
and dragged him through the streets.
And little boys were putting a shovel in his hand and saying,
"Put your sign on our document,
O Lord!"
And thus they mocked him,
until the Turks came, took him, and buried him.
And in this same year there was a terrible famine,
and a pestilence was devastating the whole land.
And in the year 1492
of the Greeks,
which is the year 576
of the Arabs,
Saladin went to war against Sultan Qilij Arslan,
on account of Nur al-Din, son of Qara Arslan, son of Dawud, son of Artuq, lord of Hisn Kayfa.
For this man was the son-in-law of Sultan Qilij Arslan,
and he had mistreated the Sultan's daughter greatly,
and brought a prostitute in over her.
And when he threatened him,
he was afraid and sought refuge with Saladin.
And this Saladin sent an envoy to the Sultan,
and requested of him to forgive his son-in-law's offense.
And when the Sultan did not accept,
Saladin made peace with the Franks of the seacoast,
and gathered his armies,
and went to the territory of Aleppo,
and encamped in the meadow called Qara Hisar (Qarahisar),
which is the blue river {Gök Su} that lies between Beth Hesna and Hisn Mansur.
And from there he went and encamped on the river Lugasu (Lugsu,
Goksu {?}),
and Nur al-Din son of Qara Arslan came to him,
and was received with honor.
Then God put peace into the heart of Sultan Qilij Arslan,
and he sent an envoy to Saladin.
And he made peace with his son-in-law, after making him swear
that he would no longer live profligately,
and that he would treat the Sultan's daughter with honor,
and submit to him like a son to his father.
And Saladin set out from there and went and encamped on the Black River (Nahr al-Aswad).
And his armies entered to plunder the land of Cilicia,
because Rupen (or Ruben?), ruler of Cilicia, had killed many of the Turkmen shepherds who were in his land,
and had captured their women, their children, and their cattle.
Rupen, however, sent words of submission and subjugation to Saladin,
and also gave much gold,
and released five hundred prisoners
